source_title: Integration of Hydrothermal Carbonisation and Anaerobic Digestion for the Energy Valorisation of Grass
authors: Aaron E. Brown; James M. Hammerton; Miller Alonso Camargo-Valero; Andrew B. Ross
geography: University of Leeds campus, United Kingdom; grass collected August 2018
evidence_class: Primary experimental literature; BMP measurements and author-calculated theoretical/biodegradability values
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), confirmed for article and University of Leeds supporting dataset
measurement_basis: Grass clippings were oven-dried at 60 °C, milled below 1 mm, and hydrothermally treated using 20 g dry grass with 200 mL distilled water (10 wt% solids), 60 min at 150, 200 or 250 °C. Approximate pressure was 4, 14 or 43 bar, respectively. BMP assays were at 37 °C for 30 days; gas volumes normalized to STP (1 atm, 0 °C, dry). Process-water methane yields are per g COD; solid-grass control is per g VS.
uncertainty: The article states EBMP analyses were performed in duplicate (n=2). Table 6 provides means but no numeric uncertainty; Figure 5 error bars show minimum and maximum values. No ranges are reconstructed here. The theoretical process-water reference is 350 NmL CH4/g COD at STP.
conversion_and_scaling: No measurement conversion performed. Source-reported units and bases are retained. The BI values are source-calculated as EBMP/TBMP; theoretical BMP is kept separate from measured BMP.
applicability: A literature comparator for grass-derived HTC process water and untreated grass BMP in a separate biorefinery context; useful for contrasting upstream conditioning and batch-digestion outcomes.
limitations: This source studies dried campus grass and HTC process water, not harvested roadside grass, press juice, brown juice, or post-protein residual.
Batch BMP is not continuous-reactor performance and does not provide a GreenHub kinetic coefficient.
The process is hydrothermal carbonization at high temperature and pressure; this technology is not an active GreenHub route.
Theoretical BMP and biodegradability index are source calculations, not independent measured observations.
No runtime input, default, TEA/LCA factor, or route is activated by this reference extract.
